script.text: Cellular respiration is how your cells get usable energy out of food. Everything else in these notes hangs off that one job.
Your notes split it into three stages. The first is glycolysis, in the cytoplasm.
The second is the Krebs cycle, in the mitochondria. The third is the electron transport chain.
So before we go on: which of the three stages happens in the cytoplasm?
Glycolysis. That is the only one outside the mitochondria, which is worth hanging on to.
The last stage makes most of the A T P. About thirty-four, according to your notes.
And where does most of that A T P come from?
The electron transport chain, the third stage. Thirty-four of them.
Three stages, in order: glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, the electron transport chain, with the energy stacked at the end.
